results.statement: Every phase-i deliverable is a targeted addition that addresses a named GitHub issue from #193-#204; nothing is added that those issues do not require.
results.context: planning session; Draft wording by flint from Rand directive 2026-10-10; wording approved by Rand 2026-10-10; source words: "I do NOT want unauthorized additions beyond what is required to address the issues filed. / These should all be line item targeted additions not redesign"
results.deterministic_check: every deliverable in every sprint bead cites one issue from #193-#204; each sprint PR diff is additive and confined to what that issue names

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.

criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.
criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.

addressed.instructions: What each issue asks: #193 first install never overwrites a consumer file (exit 2 with the paths); CI uses the vendored action ./plugins/sc-lint/.github/actions/setup-sc-lint; no action files when ci.enabled is false. #194 kit justfile has no set/default; install key justfile.windows_shell renders set windows-shell only if the consumer has none; install.py --dry-run runs just --list and exits 2 naming collisions; the kit skill's migration covers lint/test/default/set. #200 sc-lint lint <analyzer> exits nonzero on status fail; the bootstrap exports SC_LINT_BIN and puts the managed binary first on PATH. #201 each analyzer reads [tool.sc-lint.analyzers.<name>] with enabled, reason, exclude_rules, fail_rules, exclude_paths plus its own keys, unknown keys are errors; --rule-filter on every backend, forwarded by sc-lint lint; the kit renders and publishes the keys. #202 portability reads config_home_env and unix_path_prefixes (shared by PORT-001 and PORT-006) from [tool.sc-lint.analyzers.portability]. #203 boundary inventory: lib target name from cargo metadata, opaque [extensions.<namespace>] per record, allowed_dev_dependencies. #204 SCB-CYCLE-002/003: record the callee, exclude private-helper and receiver delegation unless in a multi-node cycle, exclude enum-variant expressions. Does every deliverable in `item.text` name one of these issues and do something that issue asks for, or that the code change for it strictly needs (tests, the one doc that states the changed contract, a compile fix)?

criteria.yes: Every deliverable names an issue and is required by it or strictly needed to implement it.
criteria.no: At least one deliverable names no issue or does something none of the issues asks for.
criteria.unclear: The deliverables are too vague to compare with the issues.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` add work none of #193-#204 asks for? Examples: refactors or renames not needed by the change; new traits, registries or abstractions beyond what the change needs; extra flags or options; process artifacts (gate matrices, ledgers, approval rows, certificates); documentation beyond the contract the change alters. A test, a compile-required edit, or a helper the issue's change directly calls is not extra work. Silence is not a contradiction.

criteria.yes: The item plans at least one such addition.
criteria.no: The item plans no such addition.
criteria.unclear: The item might plan such an addition but the text is ambiguous.
